Question_text: STH is an ethical business. It manufactures beds. The beds are produced in batches of 10 by employees working in teams. Delegation is encouraged so employees can reach the higher levels of Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs. All teams need to communicate regularly with management. The Operations Manager is worried as the level of wasted materials has increased over the past 3 months. She wants to improve efficiency and has identified two options; increasing training or introducing automation.
Unit: ['UNIT 2: People in business', 'UNIT 4: Operations management', 'UNIT 6: External influences on business activity']
Topic: ['2.2 Organisation and management', '2.1 Motivating employees', '2.4 Internal and external communication', '4.1 Production of goods and services', '2.3 Recruitment, selection and training of employees', '6.2 Environmental and ethical issues']
Sub_topic: Importance of delegation, trust vs control
Concept of human needs, Maslow’s hierarchy
Benefits, limitations of methods, including IT
Features, benefits, limitations: job, batch, flow production
Increasing efficiency: automation, technology, labour skills
Importance of training to business, employees
Benefits, limitations: induction, on-the-job, off-the-job training
Ethical issues: profit vs ethics conflicts

Do you think increasing training is a better way for a manufacturing business to improve efficiency than introducing automation? Justify your answer.
